story_type: crew trapped inside a capsized car carrier, pulled out through the hull
hook: Four crewmen were still alive inside this overturned ship.
narration: Four crewmen were still alive somewhere inside this overturned ship.
The Golden Ray was a six hundred fifty six foot car carrier, in St. Simons Sound, near Brunswick, Georgia.
That September morning, it was reported disabled, listing, and on fire.
Coast Guard helicopter and boat crews rescued twenty of the twenty four people aboard. Four were unaccounted for.
The next morning, the Coast Guard carried salvage crews out to the ship to check its hull.
[short pause] Around one in the afternoon, they confirmed all four were still alive inside.
On a ship lying on its side, decks become walls and stairways run sideways.
Responders made a plan. Around three, the first three crew members came out.
The fourth and final one came out at five fifty that evening.
A Coast Guard Station Brunswick boat crew brought them to shore.
outcome: All four came out alive, and every one of the twenty four people aboard the Golden Ray was rescued.
title: Trapped inside a capsized car carrier
description:
The 656-foot car carrier Golden Ray overturned in St. Simons Sound near Brunswick, Georgia, on Sept. 8, 2019. Twenty people were rescued that day, and on Sept. 9 Coast Guard and salvage crews pulled the last four crew members out of the hull alive.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video courtesy of PADET Jacksonville, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/709028/coast-guard-port-partners-salvage-crews-locate-and-rescue-four-remaining-golden-ray-crew-members-st-simons-sound

question_comment: Could you stay calm trapped inside a ship on its side, waiting for someone to knock?

extra_sources.excerpt: Salvage crews were transported by Coast Guard to the vessel at 8:22 a.m. to assess the vessel's hull and at approximately 1 p.m., Monday, it was confirmed the remaining four crew members were still alive inside the Golden Ray and an extraction plan was developed to safely rescue them.
Three crew members were safely extracted from the vessel at approximately 3 p.m. and the fourth and final crew member was safely extracted at 5:50 p.m.
The crewmembers were transported by a Coast Guard Station Brunswick 45-foot Response Boat-Medium boat crew to Glenn County EMS for further medical evaluation.
The Golden Ray had 24 people on board and 20 of the 24 people have been rescued with 4 unaccounted for.
Coast Guard boat crews, helicopter aircrews and other port partners rescued 20 people and the remaining 4 crew members were rescued Sept. 9. All 24 people on board the Golden Ray were rescued.
